For a 50-person Indian company, I’d compare the strongest realistic options as Yatra for Business, FCM Travel India, and Amex/Amex GBT. The key point: these are generally quote-based services, so there is no reliable public “₹X per employee” price to compare.

	Yatra for Business	FCM Travel India	Amex / Amex GBT
Likely cost structure	Transaction fees + actual fare/hotel cost; negotiated corporate fares	Negotiated TMC/service fees + travel cost	TMC fees + travel cost; BTA/payment solution may have separate terms
Published price	No fixed fee; transaction fee disclosed electronically 
Yatra.com
	Quote-based	Quote-based
Cancellation	Corporate fares can offer free rescheduling; cancellation at “minimal cost,” but supplier rules still apply 
Yatra.com
+1
	Supplier cancellation/change charges can apply, potentially up to 100% of booking value 
FCM Travel
	Airline/supplier cancellation rules apply; refunds can take up to 8 weeks 
American Express

Warranty / guarantee	No product-style warranty; service governed by T&Cs	No product warranty; service/support commitment instead	No travel-product warranty; supplier terms govern
Support	Online support; domestic flights 09:00–23:59 
Yatra.com
	24/7 emergency assistance and 24/7 traveller support 
FCM Travel
+1
	24/7 assistance; BTA also provides travel-insurance benefits up to ₹30 lakh, subject to exclusions 
American Express

Other value	Flights, hotels, rail, bus, cars, visas + approvals/MIS	Global inventory, negotiated hotel rates, duty-of-care and risk tools	Centralised air billing, reconciliation and potentially up to 51 days payment period 
American Express
What I’d put into the RFP

For 50 employees, don't compare only the booking fee. Ask each provider for an all-in annual quote based on the same assumptions:

500 / 1,000 / 1,500 annual trips

Domestic vs international split

Air + hotel + ground transport

Booking fee per transaction

Cancellation/change/reissue fee

Out-of-hours assistance fee

GST treatment

Credit/payment terms

Refund turnaround SLA

Dedicated account manager

24/7 emergency support

Implementation/setup fee

Any minimum annual commitment

Important: FCM's cancellation language is materially worth checking because supplier penalties can reach 100% in some cases. Yatra's corporate fares specifically advertise free rescheduling on qualifying bookings. 
Yatra.com
+1

For a 50-person company, Yatra is positioned specifically for the mid-sized segment (<2,500 trips or ₹5 crore annual travel spend), while FCM provides a more full-service TMC setup with 24/7 support. 
Yatra.com
+1

If you give me your rough annual travel spend (e.g. ₹25L/₹50L/₹1Cr), I can turn this into a realistic ₹/year total-cost model for all three.

For a 50-person Indian company, I’d compare the economics this way. The biggest issue is that travel “cost” is mostly fare + supplier penalties + TMC/service fees, not a fixed subscription.

Option	Core fees	Cancellation / changes	Support	Best fit
ITILITE	No platform fee; travel is usage-based. India pricing is quoted after spend tier; no minimum commitment. 
Itilite
+1
	Supplier fare/hotel penalties and fare differences apply. ITILITE says no extra fee for support or modifications within the same trip. 
Itilite
	24/7 human support included; dedicated AM from Growth tier. 
Itilite
	Best balance for a 50-person company
MakeMyTrip myBiz	Custom service fee + fare/hotel price + GST; 1.5% payment-gateway fee can apply to wallet/card payments. 
MakeMyTrip
	Depends heavily on airline/hotel. Selected myBiz fares offer free cancellation/date changes. 
MakeMyTrip Biz
	Primarily platform-led support	Best for India-heavy domestic travel
FCM Travel	Custom TMC quote; no public standard price.	Supplier cancellation/reissue rules apply; cancellation can reach 100% of booking value. Refunds may wait until supplier funds arrive. 
FCM Travel
	24/7 support, travel manager, duty-of-care and emergency assistance. 
FCM Travel
+1
	Best for complex/international travel
OfficeKit HR Platinum	Custom per-user/month quote; Platinum includes travel management. 
OfficeKit HR
	Travel-provider rules apply; don't treat the HRMS subscription as cancellation protection.	HRMS/support model rather than a dedicated TMC	Best if you also need HR/payroll
What I'd ask for in the quote

For 50 employees, get each provider to quote 100 domestic flight bookings + 50 hotel nights + 20 cancellations/changes. That exposes the real TCO much better than the headline subscription.

Also specifically request: booking fee, reissue fee, cancellation fee, GST/ITC handling, unused-ticket credits, 24/7 support SLA, implementation fee, and any annual minimum spend.
